"You Could Hear It Everywhere" R. M., Cleveland I swear every place I went this year had "Stayin' Alive" playing at least once. I didn't mind. It felt like the city had one shared soundtrack. "Two Songs, Same Family" D. P., Sacramento Between Bee Gees and Andy Gibb showing up all over the list, this year felt like one long musical conversation. I love hearing how those songs sat next to each other. "Give Me the Slow Burn" L. H., Tulsa The flashy hits were great, but I kept returning to songs that stayed for months. Those long runs tell the real story of what people lived with. "Movie Songs on the Radio" J. F., Newark When "You're The One That I Want" and "Grease" kept climbing, it made movie nights feel like part of radio nights. That's the crossover I remember. "Thanks for the Top 23" S. K., Phoenix Love the closing countdown page idea. It feels like the final spin before the station signs off for the night.
